messages:
alex_kim: FYI we just got a DSAR from an EU user asking for full deletion + proof. They explicitly asked to remove all context, embeddings, and any snapshots. Also they want confirmation that KMS-wrapped keys won't retain access.

mira_patel: thanks — can you paste the request (redact PII) and whether there's an active retention exception on their org?

alex_kim: pasted in the ticket (link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/DSAR-1123). short summary: requester = EU resident, asks deletion of chat + embeddings; legal hold = none; retention exception = a manual tag exists on bucket `eu-embeddings-prod` from last year (ticket RET-88).

security-bot: automated check: embeddings index "eu-vec-prod" has 1.2M vectors, primary storage is third-party vector DB (pinecone) with metadata pointers to s3://eu-embeddings-prod, snapshots in backups account eu-backups, KMS key alias: alias/redwood/eu-emb-kms. No active legal hold detected in Jira.

drew: quick questions: (1) do we have a delete path that removes vector entries + s3 objects + backup snapshots? (2) do we need to rotate / rewrap the DEK so old snapshots can't be decrypted? (3) who can run the delete — ops or support?

mira_patel: all good Qs. Our current delete flow: 1) remove vector id from pinecone index via API; 2) delete object from s3 prefix `users/<hashed-id>/`; 3) mark associated DB rows as deleted (logical). Backups/snapshots are retained per policy and require retention-exception override to remove. For KMS: objects are encrypted with a DEK wrapped by CMK `alias/redwood/eu-emb-kms`. Rotating CMK doesn't retroactively make past snapshots unrecoverable if you keep the wrapped DEKs. To ensure irrecoverability we need to delete the wrapped DEK metadata and purge backups or remove KMS key material (not trivial).

ops_sre: we must follow forensics process before any irreversible deletion. if legal doesn't require preserving artifacts, we still snapshot a forensics image to secure air-gapped storage and then delete. I can create an immutable snapshot and hand it to legal/forensics for 90 days. that buys us a defensible copy.

elaine_legal: confirm requester verification steps: we need government ID + registered email confirmation. once identity is confirmed we can proceed. also we can't delete data if there's an open subpoena or ongoing investigation. none present per my check.

alex_kim: action items I'm proposing: (A) draw up deletion plan that covers pinecone + s3 + backups + KMS considerations, (B) request temporary RBAC grant to a dsar-deleter role, (C) ops creates forensics snapshot, (D) legal verifies identity, (E) security signs off on vuln/attack surface. any objections?

drew: on RBAC: we should avoid broad permanent grants. propose creating a short-lived role `dsar-deleter:DSAR-1123` with scoped perms limited to pinecone-delete, s3-delete for the specific prefix, and rds-update on the rows. TTL 8 hours. I can provision that and record the grant in audit logs.

security-bot: recommended audit events to capture: `audit.event:subject_request.delete.requested`, `audit.principal:dsar-deleter:DSAR-1123`, `audit.target:pinecone:eu-vec-prod`, `audit.s3.prefix:users/<hashed-id>`, `audit.kms.key:alias/redwood/eu-emb-kms`, `audit.result:SUCCESS|FAIL`. ensure logs are immutable and shipped to sec-logs for retention.

mira_patel: regarding KMS: ops will need to unwrap the DEK to delete s3 objects if we want to verify content before deletion. alternatively, if we simply delete the s3 object and associated wrapped-DEK metadata, restoring from backup could still allow decryption if wrapped-DEKs exist. recommendation: delete object + delete wrapped-DEK entry in our metadata store and then request deletion of backups that contain the wrapped DEK. note: some backup providers keep their own encrypted copies; coordinate with vendor.

ops_sre: vendor note — pinecone supports tombstoning vector ids; however their backups are retained 30 days. we'll need to request them to purge specific ids under DSAR legal process. I'm looped in with vendor ops and can escalate.

elaine_legal: for proof of deletion we typically provide: (1) audit log snippets showing deletion API calls, (2) confirmation from third-party (pinecone) that ids were purged, (3) confirmation of s3 object deletion and backup purge requests, (4) statement about key material and irrecoverability. We need all of that before we mark request complete.

alex_kim: there's one more thing — during a quick review I flagged a low-severity vuln in the support tool used to map user IDs to vector prefixes: it allowed a support token to query arbitrary prefixes if a param was malformed. not exploited AFAICT. marking this for triage — can we run a quick patch before deletion so we don't create an audit gap?

security-bot: vulnerability triage checklist: assign CVE? no. severity: low-medium. Reproduce steps, patch, test in staging. If patch affects deletion flow, coordinate window with DSAR timeline.

drew: I'll create the temporary role and the least-privilege IAM policy now, post the ARN here once ready. will also tag the grant with `dsar:1123` for audit. ETA 2h.

ops_sre: I'll create the forensics snapshot and open the vendor purge ticket with pinecone. also will coordinate with backups team to locate any snapshots that include the user's objects; may need retention-exception reversal on RET-88 to purge. ETA for snapshot: 4h; vendor response unknown.

elaine_legal: I'm verifying identity now. if verified, we can proceed with the deletion steps and provide the standard proof bundle. please hold until I confirm. ETA 24h for identity docs.

mira_patel: noted. security sign-off needed before actual delete. I'll draft the deletion playbook with explicit steps and checklist (pre-delete snapshot, RBAC role creation, vendor purge requests, delete calls, post-delete audit bundle). I'll share draft in this thread in ~3h.

alex_kim: thanks all. summary: hold until legal confirms identity, drew/ops to prep RBAC + snapshot, mira to draft playbook, security to triage vuln in parallel. target: complete within 48h after identity confirmed. tagging @here for visibility. :white_check_mark:
